title: Low Rank Multi-Dictionary Selection at Scale

problem.claim: Scale multi-dictionary coding to large dictionaries and datasets.

gap.claim: Large and over-complete dictionaries create scalability challenges that are worsened in multi-dictionary settings.

contributions.claim: LRMDS progressively selects groups of row-column atom pairs according to their alignment with the data and performs convex-relaxation coding using the corresponding sub-dictionaries.
Under mild assumptions, LRMDS can select a sparse subset of atoms when the data has a low-rank encoding, with strong guarantees.
LRMDS is evaluated on synthetic and real-world datasets across multiple coding dictionaries.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report theoretical and experimental evidence for atom-selection guarantees under mild assumptions.
The authors report scalability and quality evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets and across a range of coding dictionaries.
The authors report 3-to-10-times speed-ups over baselines and up to two orders of magnitude better representation quality on some real-world datasets at a fixed target number of atoms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sparse dictionary coding represents signals using a small number of predefined dictionary atoms and has been applied across several data types.
Large over-complete dictionaries, especially in multi-dictionary settings, create scalability problems.
The paper introduces LRMDS, which progressively selects aligned row-column atom pairs and codes using corresponding sub-dictionaries.
The authors report theoretical guarantees, synthetic and real-world evaluations, speed-ups, and representation-quality improvements.

source_observation.claim: Progressive selection of atom-pair groups is used to address scalability in large multi-dictionary coding.

interpretation.claim: Restricting computation to progressively selected sub-dictionaries may reduce the cost of coding with large over-complete dictionaries.

application.claim: For large structured dictionaries, consider alignment-based progressive subset selection before solving the coding problem.

exception.claim: The reported guarantees rely on low-rank encoding, sparse atom support, and mild assumptions.

unknowns: The specific mild assumptions and form of the theoretical guarantees are not provided.
The baseline methods, dataset sizes, experimental configurations, and conditions for the reported improvements are not provided.
The abstract does not specify the exact convex relaxation or atom-selection objective.
